title.back: Section check: Truth, power and choices
title.note: The section's Indonesian title from course.json.

intro.source: 10 questions about Lessons 13–17. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 10 questions about Lessons 13–17. No need to hurry. You may look at the lessons again and try again as often as you like.

questions.0.question.source: A picture has an extra finger. Why is that only a clue, not proof, that AI made it?
questions.0.question.back: A picture has an extra finger. Why is that only a clue, not proof, that AI made it?

questions.0.options.0.text.source: Only artists can spot an extra finger
questions.0.options.0.text.back: Only artists can see an extra finger

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Anyone can spot it. But real photos can look strange too. Look back at Lesson 13.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Anyone can see it. But real photos can look strange too. Look at Lesson 13 again.

questions.0.options.1.text.source: Real photos can look odd too
questions.0.options.1.text.back: Real photos can look strange too

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Real photos can look strange, for example in poor light. And newer AI tools make fewer mistakes.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. Real photos can look strange, for example in poor light. And newer AI tools make fewer mistakes.

questions.0.options.2.text.source: AI tools never make that kind of mistake
questions.0.options.2.text.back: AI tools never make a mistake like that

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. AI pictures sometimes have an extra finger. But a real photo can look odd too. Look back at Lesson 13.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. AI pictures sometimes have an extra finger. But a real photo can look odd too. Look at Lesson 13 again.

questions.1.question.source: In a 2025 study, more than 50,000 people judged real photos and AI pictures. What did it find?
questions.1.question.back: In a 2025 study, more than 50,000 people judged real photos and AI-made pictures. What did it find?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: People made many mistakes, both ways
questions.1.options.0.text.back: People were often wrong, in both directions
questions.1.options.0.text.note: “People made many mistakes, both ways” → “Orang sering salah, di kedua arah” (people were often wrong, in both directions); Lesson 13's teachers' note says “di setiap arah”.

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. They called about one in four real photos AI-made. They also missed about one in four AI pictures.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. They called about one in four real photos AI-made. They also did not recognise about one in four AI pictures.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: People spotted almost every AI picture
questions.1.options.1.text.back: People recognised almost every AI picture

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. They missed about one in four AI pictures. Look back at Lesson 13.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. They did not recognise about one in four AI pictures. Look at Lesson 13 again.

questions.1.options.2.text.source: Real photos were always easy to tell
questions.1.options.2.text.back: Real photos were always easy to recognise

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. People called about one in four real photos AI-made. Look back at Lesson 13.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. People called about one in four real photos AI-made. Look at Lesson 13 again.

questions.2.question.source: “The bridge closes for a whole year” is a claim. What is a claim?
questions.2.question.back: “The bridge is closed for a whole year” is a claim. What is a claim?

questions.2.options.0.text.source: A fact that has already been checked
questions.2.options.0.text.back: A fact whose truth has already been checked
questions.2.options.0.text.note: Lengthened a little (“whose truth has already been checked”) so the three options are of similar length.

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A claim may not be checked yet. It may be true or false. Look back at Lesson 14.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A claim may not have been checked yet. A claim can be true or false. Look at Lesson 14 again.

questions.2.options.1.text.source: A post that many people have shared
questions.2.options.1.text.back: A post that many people have shared

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Sharing does not make something a claim, or make it true. Look back at Lesson 14.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Being shared does not make something a claim, or make it true. Look at Lesson 14 again.

questions.2.options.2.text.source: Something a person says is true
questions.2.options.2.text.back: Something a person says is the truth
questions.2.options.2.text.note: Lesson 14's glossary definition of “klaim” (“Sesuatu yang dikatakan seseorang sebagai kebenaran”), with “Hal” for “Sesuatu”.

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. A claim is something a person says is true. It may be true or false, so you check it.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. A claim is something a person says is the truth. A claim can be true or false, so you check it.

questions.3.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. In the made-up town of Rockford, a page with no name posts: “The market closes forever on Monday. Share this before they delete it.” There is no link and no evidence. Three other pages copy the post word for word.
questions.3.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. In the made-up town of Rockford, a page with no name posts: “The market closes forever on Monday. Share this before they delete it.” There is no link and no evidence. Three other pages copy the post word for word.

questions.3.question.source: Which source would best show if the post is true?
questions.3.question.back: Which source can best show whether the post is true?

questions.3.options.0.text.source: The town office that runs the market
questions.3.options.0.text.back: The town office that runs the market

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The office runs the market, so it knows the plans. Check what it says before you share.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. The office runs the market, so the office knows the plans. Check what it says before you share.

questions.3.options.1.text.source: The three pages that copied the post
questions.3.options.1.text.back: The three pages that copied the post

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Copies add no evidence. Four copies are still one source. Look back at Lesson 14.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Copies add no evidence. Four copies are still just one source. Look at Lesson 14 again.

questions.3.options.2.text.source: How many times the post was shared
questions.3.options.2.text.back: How many times the post was shared

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A shocking post can be shared a lot and still be false. Look back at Lesson 14.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A shocking post can be shared a lot and still be false. Look at Lesson 14 again.

questions.4.question.source: Some people worry that a feed shows each of us only one side of things. What is this called?
questions.4.question.back: Some people worry that a feed shows each of us only one side of things. What is this situation called?

questions.4.options.0.text.note: “A news alert” → “Notifikasi berita” (a news notification), what phones call it in Indonesian.

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A news alert tells you about one new story. It is not about seeing only one side. Look back at Lesson 15.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A news notification tells you about one new story. It is not about seeing only one side. Look at Lesson 15 again.

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. In a filter bubble, you only see one side. A 2022 review found that real bubbles are less common than many think.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. Inside a filter bubble, you only see one side. A 2022 review found that real bubbles are rarer than many people think.

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. An algorithm is a set of steps that picks posts. It is not the one-sided feed itself. Look back at Lesson 15.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. An algorithm is a series of steps that picks posts. An algorithm is not the one-sided feed itself. Look at Lesson 15 again.

questions.5.question.source: In Maplebrook, a post said the vote had moved to Friday. It got 900 shares. The election office's post got 60. What does this show?
questions.5.question.back: In Maplebrook, a post said the vote had been moved to Friday. That post was shared 900 times. The election office's post was shared 60 times. What does this show?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: Most people checked the post before sharing it
questions.5.options.0.text.back: Most people checked the post before sharing it

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The false post got far more shares than the true ones. Look back at Lesson 15.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The false post was shared far more than the true post. Look at Lesson 15 again.

questions.5.options.1.text.source: The vote really did move to Friday
questions.5.options.1.text.back: The vote really was moved to Friday

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The election office and the fact-checkers say the vote is still on Saturday. Look back at Lesson 15.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The election office and the fact-checkers say the vote is still on Saturday. Look at Lesson 15 again.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: A rumour can spread further than the truth
questions.5.options.2.text.back: A rumour can spread further than the truth

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. The rumour had no name and no link, but it got far more shares than the true post.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. The rumour had no name and no link, but it was shared far more than the true post.

questions.6.question.source: How does the European Union's AI Act sort the ways AI is used?
questions.6.question.back: How does the European Union's AI Act sort the ways AI is used?
questions.6.question.note: “AI Act” kept as Lesson 16 names it (“AI Act (undang-undang AI) milik UE”).

questions.6.options.0.text.source: By how much harm they could do
questions.6.options.0.text.back: By how big their danger is
questions.6.options.0.text.note: “By how much harm they could do” → “Menurut seberapa besar bahayanya” (by how big their danger is), Lesson 16's simpler wording for risk; shorter so the correct option is not the longest.

questions.6.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The law sorts uses by risk. Some uses are banned, and some need strict checks.
questions.6.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. The law sorts uses of AI by their risk. Some uses are banned, and some others need strict checks.

questions.6.options.1.text.source: By which company made the tool
questions.6.options.1.text.back: By the company that made the tool

questions.6.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The law looks at risk: how much harm a use could do. Look back at Lesson 16.
questions.6.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The law looks at risk: how much harm a use could cause. Look at Lesson 16 again.

questions.6.options.2.text.source: By how new or old each tool is
questions.6.options.2.text.back: By how new or old the tool is

questions.6.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Age does not matter in this law. It sorts uses by risk. Look back at Lesson 16.
questions.6.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A tool's age does not matter in this law. The law sorts uses by risk. Look at Lesson 16 again.

questions.7.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. The council of the made-up town of Lakeford plans a chatbot to answer questions at night. A student group is getting ready for the town meeting. They write down questions to look into.
questions.7.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. The council of Lakeford, a made-up town, plans to use a chatbot to answer questions at night. A group of students is getting ready for the town's residents' meeting. They write down questions they want to look into.
questions.7.stimulus.body.note: “town meeting” → “pertemuan warga kota” (town residents' meeting); the title says “Pertemuan warga rekaan”.

questions.7.question.source: Which of their questions asks for a recommendation, not a fact?
questions.7.question.back: Which of their questions asks for a recommendation, not a fact?
questions.7.question.note: “recommendation” → “usulan” (proposal), the word Lesson 16 uses for “what should Hillford do?”.

questions.7.options.0.text.source: Since 2026, what must EU chatbots make clear?
questions.7.options.0.text.back: Since 2026, what must chatbots in the EU make clear?

questions.7.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The EU law gives a factual answer: a chatbot must make clear that it is a machine. Look back at Lesson 16.
questions.7.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The EU law gives an answer that is a fact: a chatbot must make clear that it is a machine. Look at Lesson 16 again.

questions.7.options.1.text.source: Should Lakeford's chatbot work at night?
questions.7.options.1.text.back: Should Lakeford's chatbot work at night?
questions.7.options.1.text.note: “Perlukah …?” (does … need to / should …?), a short natural question form.

questions.7.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. This asks what Lakeford should do. Your view can be different from any law, if you give reasons.
questions.7.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. This question asks what Lakeford should do. Your view may differ from any law, as long as you give reasons.

questions.7.options.2.text.source: Is the ASEAN guide a law or a guideline?
questions.7.options.2.text.back: Is the ASEAN guide a law or a guideline?

questions.7.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. This has a factual answer: the ASEAN guide is a guideline. Look back at Lesson 16.
questions.7.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. This question has an answer that is a fact: the ASEAN guide is a guideline. Look at Lesson 16 again.

questions.8.question.source: What would a project need to show impact?
questions.8.question.back: What does a project need to show impact?

questions.8.options.0.text.source: A prize from a big group of judges
questions.8.options.0.text.back: A prize from a big group of judges

questions.8.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A prize shows that judges liked an idea. It does not show that life got better. Look back at Lesson 17.
questions.8.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A prize shows that the judges liked an idea. A prize does not show that life became better. Look at Lesson 17 again.

questions.8.options.1.text.source: A first working version of it
questions.8.options.1.text.back: A first version of the project that already works

questions.8.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. That is a prototype. Impact comes later, if there is evidence that it helps. Look back at Lesson 17.
questions.8.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. That is a prototype. Impact comes later, if there is evidence that the project helps. Look at Lesson 17 again.

questions.8.options.2.text.source: Evidence that it made life better
questions.8.options.2.text.back: Evidence that life became better because of it
questions.8.options.2.text.note: “Evidence that it made life better” → “Bukti bahwa hidup menjadi lebih baik karenanya” (evidence that life became better because of it).

questions.8.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Impact is the real difference a project makes. SELENA+ does not have that evidence yet.
questions.8.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. Impact is the real change a project makes. SELENA+ does not have that evidence yet.

questions.9.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. At the made-up Elm Street Centre, many visitors get lost in the big building. Pita wants to build an AI helper to guide them. Noor says, “Clear signs on the walls might work better.”
questions.9.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. At the made-up Elm Street Centre, many visitors get lost in the big building. Pita wants to make an AI helper to guide them. Noor says, “Clear signboards on the walls might work better.”
questions.9.stimulus.body.note: “Elm Street Centre” → “Pusat Elm Street”, name kept and “Centre” translated, as TERMS does for Hillview Learning Centre. “signs” is “papan petunjuk” (signboards), as TERMS says for Lesson 17.

questions.9.question.source: What does Lesson 17 say about Noor's idea?
questions.9.question.back: What does Lesson 17 say about Noor's idea?

questions.9.options.0.text.source: A simpler plan can be a strong design
questions.9.options.0.text.back: A simpler plan can be a strong design

questions.9.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. First decide if AI should be used at all. A sign, a rule or a person can be a better answer.
questions.9.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. First, decide whether AI needs to be used at all. A signboard, a rule or a person can be a better answer.

questions.9.options.1.text.source: Every good design needs to use AI
questions.9.options.1.text.back: Every good design must always use AI

questions.9.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The lesson says a sign, a simple rule or a person can be better. Look back at Lesson 17.
questions.9.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The lesson says a signboard, a simple rule or a person can be better. Look at Lesson 17 again.

questions.9.options.2.text.source: Signs are only for very small buildings
questions.9.options.2.text.back: Signboards are only for very small buildings

questions.9.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The lesson says a simpler plan, with reasons, is a strong design. Look back at Lesson 17.
questions.9.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The lesson says a simpler plan, with reasons, is a strong design. Look at Lesson 17 again.

results.high.source: Well done. You know how to check what you see, and how people make rules and plans for AI.
results.high.back: Very good. You know how to check what you see, and how people make rules and plans for AI.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Good work. You answered many questions correctly. Look at the lessons again for the questions whose answers were not quite right, then try again if you want.

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 13–17, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Look at Lessons 13–17 again, then try again. You may use as much time as you need.
